source.quote: Musical Fidelity's own page for the M8x DAC, read 2026-11-25. « 1x Asynchronous USB: up to 768kHz »; « USB PCM sample rates: up to 768kHz »; « USB: DSD 256 (stereo DoP), DSD512 (stereo native) »; « USB DSD support: up to DSD256 via DoP and native DSD512 »; « 3x Optical input: up to 24bit / PCM 192kHz, MQA 384kHz, DoP DSD 64 »; « 1x Coaxial input: up to 24bit / PCM 192kHz, MQA 384kHz, DoP DSD 64 »; « 1x AES/EBU input: 1x up to 24bit / PCM 192kHz, MQA 384kHz, DoP DSD 64 »; « DAC chip: 2x ES9038Q2M (dual mono) with 8x digital filter »; « Selectable Digital Filters »; « For PCM signals, the M8x DAC has eight selectable digital filters. »; « Switchable Upsampling »; « Oversampling Bypass ». No bit depth is stated for the USB input. musicalfidelity.com's terms page was READ and carries no prohibition on copying or reusing site content - its only restrictive clause names « unauthorised framing » - and the footer reads « Copyright Musical Fidelity 2026 ».

device_settings.why: « Oversampling Bypass » is a named feature beside « Switchable Upsampling » and « Selectable Digital Filters ». Switching the oversampling out puts the device's own interpolation stage out of the path, which is what Auto needs and what makes `correctable` true. The eight PCM filters only matter if the bypass is off.

« For PCM signals, the M8x DAC has eight selectable digital filters » and not one is named - the tenth maker in three days to publish a count and withhold the list. The Topping DX1 II's manual names eight of what is very probably the same ESS menu, and they are NOT copied here.

_un_contournement_du_sur_echantillonnage: « Oversampling Bypass », as a named feature, on a mainstream British DAC. Eight NOS or bypass devices are now recorded - FiiO twice, Schiit four times, Rockna, LampizatOr, MHDT four times - and this is the first from a maker of this kind, which matters because `correctable` has been a high-end and specialist field until now. If per-device correction is ever to reach a real number of listeners it will be through devices like this one.
_MQA_a_384_kHz_sur_des_entrees_plafonnee: « up to 24bit / PCM 192kHz, MQA 384kHz, DoP DSD 64 » on optical, coaxial and AES/EBU. The same socket is rated 192 kHz for PCM and 384 kHz for MQA, because MQA carries its higher rate folded inside a 192 kHz stream. inputs.pcm_max_hz takes 192000, which is what ordinary PCM reaches; the 384 is not a PCM ceiling and writing it would overstate every one of those three inputs by a factor of two. Fifth maker to publish MQA figures and the first where they sit in the same row as the PCM ones.
